name: Face-touching / phone hygiene habit

lead: People wipe phones, change pillowcases and avoid touching their faces hoping to reduce breakouts.
No studies reviewed test these habits directly.

paras: Proponents say it limits oil, dirt and friction against the skin; references note friction can aggravate existing acne.
No specific risks are documented; references also say over-washing is not recommended.

lead: The face-touching and phone hygiene habit refers to wiping phones, washing pillowcases and avoiding touching the face in order to reduce breakouts. It is a lifestyle routine discussed in skincare circles.

General acne references report that cleanliness is not associated with acne, that washing affected skin more than twice daily is generally not recommended, and that mechanical pressure from helmets or chinstraps can worsen existing acne (acne mechanica) [1]. They do not address phones or pillowcases specifically.

paras: Wikipedia states hygiene is not associated with acne and notes friction and occlusion can aggravate existing lesions [1]. No source reviewed examines phone contact or pillowcase washing.
